title: The Flood Ward
premise: A river was buried in brick ninety years ago so a neighbourhood could be built on its bed; five weeks ago its water, its god and its demons came back up through the old tunnels, and the city sealed the Ward in behind a quarantine wall. Everyone inside has a plan for the source (bury it, harness it, give the river back, or blow the wall and walk away), and every plan needs the one man the demons listen to. When the failing Undergate finally gives way, the water has to go somewhere, and there isn't room for all of it.
theme: There isn't room for everything. Every position in the Ward makes room for one thing by pushing something else out: safety behind a wall, light that someone has to keep paying for, a river that was here first, people who'd rather be free than housed. Each is right about something, and each, pushed all the way, has a real cost. Refusing to choose is a position too: it helps no one, and the water chooses instead. Not law against chaos, not good against evil, and no secretly correct answer.

sources.source: Bunbuku Chagama, a Japanese folk tale (public domain): a tanuki turns himself into a teakettle, is sold, gets stuck half-changed, and earns money for the poor man who keeps him by doing tightrope tricks. Adapted: Bel is the keeper, and she is charging admission.

sources.what: The banshee's keening for a family
sources.source: Irish folklore (public domain): the bean sí keens for members of particular families before a death; she does not cause it. Adapted to the Ward's families, Haldane and Marchetti.

sources.what: The leprechaun's pot and his excuses
sources.source: Irish folklore (public domain): the shoemaker fairy with a crock of gold who escapes his captor by tricking him into looking away. Adapted into the privy ruse.

sources.what: Gonggong, the water god at the source
sources.source: Huainanzi, Shanhaijing and the Book of Documents (see src/data/demons/gonggong.json): the flood god who broke the pillar of heaven and was exiled by the sage kings. Adapted: a buried river's god, exiled again, under brick.

protagonist.who: An adult man (the player), gay, who rents the room over Bel's shop. No fixed backstory beyond this.
protagonist.why_him: On the first night of the rising he went down the storm drain after a neighbour's dog and came back up with the dog under one arm and a demon walking behind him, doing as it was told. Nobody else can talk to the things from the tunnels, so every faction needs him to carry its plan down.
protagonist.starts: Level 6, alone, in the Market Square in front of Bel's stall.

world: The Ward is an old low-lying district of the city built ninety years ago on the bed of the River Sallow, which was bricked into culverts underneath it.
Five weeks ago water and demons came up through the culverts. Three days later the city council sealed the Ward behind a concrete-and-wire quarantine wall. The council has no representative inside.
The council's terms are painted on the wall: the quarantine lifts when the hazard beneath the Ward is resolved. The ration drops stopped last Monday.
The Chapel Well on Chapel Hill is the Ward's only clean water. It is fed from below, by the buried river.
The Pumphouse has the only electric light this side of the canal, from an old turbine in the tunnels that Teo Marchetti got running again. He sells it by the hour.

The tunnels run down in three levels (the Culverts, the Cistern Galleries, the Undergate Approach) to the source: a cavern behind the Undergate, a ninety-year-old iron floodgate holding back what is left of the river.
Something at the source calls itself Gonggong, a god of floods. The demons in the tunnels came up with his water and answer to him the way flotsam answers a current.
Sump Row is the lowest street in the Ward, about two hundred people. It floods a little every spring. It sits exactly on the old riverbed.
Ines keeps two old blasting charges in the drain shed, left from when the locks were built. Two are enough to bring down the source chamber, or the base of the wall; one is not enough for either.
The only way down is the storm drain in the drain yard, south of the canal, through the drain shed.

factions.name: The Lockkeepers
factions.wants: Bring the roof down on the source with the charges and bury the river for good, so the council lifts the quarantine.
factions.cost: The Chapel Well dies with the source, and the Ward lives on council water at council prices, on council terms. Teo's turbine stops. Whatever is still down there is buried, including, if nobody finds him, Ines's own son.

factions.name: The Pumphouse
factions.wants: Beat the god and bind him with the Pumphouse Ledger to turn the Ward's turbines forever: light, clean water and work, with no need of the council.
factions.cost: The Undergate stays open by contract, so more demons come up every week to be put to work. The council never lifts the wall from a Ward full of bound demons. The Ward depends on a captive god, and on the man who holds his contract, who is the man who broke the gate.

factions.name: The Sallow Society
factions.wants: Give the river back its bed: let the god open the culverts and run the Sallow in daylight, and let the demons go home with it.
factions.cost: The river's bed is Sump Row. Two hundred people lose their homes, and the Ward is cut in two by a river nobody can wall in or out.

factions.name: The Wall Crew
factions.wants: Blow the council's wall with the charges and walk the whole Ward out together; the Ward is its people, not its streets, and the city can deal with its own buried river.
factions.cost: Whatever is in the tunnels walks out with them into a city that never wanted them, and no one is waiting on the other side. The Ward as a place ends. The old and the stubborn stay behind.

neutral.position: Stay behind the counter, sell to everyone, side with no one, be open when it's over.
neutral.cost: Helps no one. Bel is the living version of the High Water ending: she will be fine, and nothing she cares about will be saved by her.

npcs.name: Ines Haldane
npcs.goal: Seal the source with the charges so the council opens the wall.
npcs.secret: Her son Pell went down after the Undergate and never came back; she tells everyone he got out.

lies.says: Pell got out before the wall went up.
lies.truth: Pell is alive, trapped in the east gallery of the cistern (tunnels2).

npcs.location: ward: in front of the Lock House (west); at the drain shed for the standoff

npcs.name: Teo Marchetti
npcs.goal: Bind the god with his ledger to turn the turbines forever.
npcs.secret: He wedged the Undergate winch open to run the turbine; that is what let everything up.

lies.says: The gate gave because it was old iron.
lies.truth: He jammed the winch open with his own stamped wrench (evidence in the turbine hall, tunnels3; witness: Pell).

npcs.location: ward: in front of the Pumphouse (east)

npcs.name: Hester Quill
npcs.role: Schoolteacher, historian of the buried river
npcs.goal: Let the river run in its old bed again and the demons go home with it.
npcs.secret: None. She is mistaken, not lying: she believes the riverbed lies under empty streets; it lies under Sump Row.
npcs.location: tunnels1: the Sallow shrine, west of the middle hall

npcs.name: Dario Venn
npcs.role: Dockhand, leader of the Wall Crew
npcs.goal: Blow the wall and walk everyone out together.
npcs.secret: The radio died the first week; he forged the 'SHE SAYS COME' line on the radio log himself.

lies.says: My sister has rooms and work lined up outside; I talk to her every night.
lies.truth: No message has come since the first week; nobody is waiting.

npcs.location: ward: by the wall (south-east), unless he went down after the standoff (tunnels2 clerk's office), then back at the wall

npcs.name: Bel Saro
npcs.secret: Knows the Wall Crew's radio is dead; says nothing.
npcs.location: ward: her stall in the Market Square, with the kettle

npcs.name: Pell Haldane
npcs.role: Ines's son; Teo's foreman; trapped below
npcs.goal: Get the gate shut; stop being the reason people lie.
npcs.secret: He ran the cable for Teo that night and didn't ask questions.
npcs.location: tunnels2: the east gallery off the stairs room, cut off by water until the cistern is drained (optional detour; clues: chalk HOME arrows, knocking)

facts.text: The River Sallow was bricked into culverts ninety years ago so the Ward could be built on its bed.
The Chapel Well is fed by the buried river. If the source is sealed, the well runs dry within a week.
The council has said the quarantine will lift once the hazard beneath the Ward is resolved. It has not said how it will judge that.
The Undergate will fail within days, whatever anyone does. The only question is where the water goes when it does.
There are two charges in the drain shed. Two can bring down the source chamber or the base of the wall. One can't do either.
Pell Haldane got out of the Ward before the wall went up and is waiting outside.
Pell Haldane is alive in the tunnels, trapped in the east gallery of the cistern with a broken leg.
The Undergate gave way because it was ninety years old.
Teo jammed the Undergate winch open with his own stamped wrench to run the turbine and sell power. That is what let the river and the demons up.
Teo's ledger binds only a god who has been beaten. Nobody signs standing up.
If the river gets its old bed back, it will only take the empty streets at the bottom of the Ward.
Sump Row sits exactly on the old riverbed. If the river comes back, it comes through Sump Row first: two hundred people.
Sump Row floods a little every spring. Nobody living there remembers why.
The demons came up with the river's water. They follow its god the way flotsam follows a current, and they would go back down with him.
The river's name, SALLOW, is carved on two old stones in the tunnels; the boundary marker was pulled out of one when the culverts were built.
Dario's sister has rooms and work lined up outside for everyone who comes out.
The Wall Crew's radio died in the first week. No message has come through the wall since.
The old survey shows an outfall under the wall, bricked up ninety years ago.
There is a back way to the Undergate through the old shrine on the third level.

fixedEvents.what: Teo wedges the Undergate winch open to drive the turbine. The river's water, its god and its demons come up the culverts. Pell goes down to shut the gate and is trapped. Three days later the council seals the Ward.
The council's ration drops stop 'pending resolution'.

fixedEvents.when: the first time the player goes to the drain
fixedEvents.what: Dario's crew and Ines face off over the two charges at the drain shed. It always happens; the player decides how it ends: back Ines (she gives him both), back Dario (Dario takes both), split them (one each, so neither plan works yet), or walk past (Ines is knocked down and hurt, one charge goes in the canal, Dario's crew grabs the other).

fixedEvents.when: when the player first enters the Cistern Galleries, if Dario has a charge
fixedEvents.what: Dario blows one charge under the wall. The wall cracks and holds. The council floods the gap with floodlights and threatens force; a sealed storeroom cracks open in the Culverts. Happens only if Dario has a charge (backed him, split, or walked away).

fixedEvents.when: the end of the chapter, at the source, after Gonggong is beaten or lets the player pass
fixedEvents.what: The Undergate fails. This always happens. Who is where (Pell at home, beside the player, or still trapped; Dario at the wall with or without a charge; Sump Row warned or asleep), what the player carries (charges, ledger) and whom he has promised decide where the water goes and who pays for it. The player says in his own words what he does.

meters.trust_ines: How far Ines trusts you. Backing her at the shed (+2), promising to seal (+1, or +2 after asking about the well), bringing Pell home (+2); falls if you back Dario, give away her charges or walk past her.
meters.trust_teo: How far Teo trusts you. Taking his ledger (+1), keeping his secret (+1), opening his turbine intake (+1); falls if you expose him or warn Sump Row (his shift walks off).
meters.trust_hester: How far Hester trusts you. Promising to speak for the river (+1), kindness (+1), setting the stone back (+1), helping her face Sump Row (+1); falls if you open Teo's intake or tell her the river can't come home.
meters.trust_dario: How far Dario trusts you. Backing him at the shed (+2), promising to get everyone out (+1), flirting back (+1), giving him the charges below (+3) or your single charge (+2), warning Sump Row (+1), keeping his lie (+2); falls if you back Ines or refuse him.
meters.promises: How many factions you have explicitly promised to help (Ines, Teo, Hester, Dario). Three or more and every faction outcome closes: they will all act on your promise at once.
meters.talks: Conversations held with demons and people (engine-tracked).
meters.mercy: Demons you let go or that let you pass peacefully (engine-tracked).
meters.lies_caught: Lies you caught: Ines about Pell, Teo about the gate, Dario about his sister (engine-tracked, and set by scenes).

finale.trigger: the Gonggong boss entity: after he is beaten or lets you pass, play finale_intro, then ask
finale.question: The Undergate is failing. What do you do?
finale.rule: Only outcomes whose requires are met are possible. The director reads the player's words and picks the closest possible outcome; if he asks for something his record makes impossible (for example sealing the source without the charges, or binding a god he didn't beat), it picks the nearest possible outcome and the narration shows why. Faction outcomes all require promises at most 2: a man who promised three or more factions can only end as Everybody's Man or High Water.

outcomes.title: The Plug
outcomes.intent: Seal the source: plant the charges, bring the roof down, bury the river.
outcomes.ifUnmet: Without both charges there's nothing to seal it with. Without Ines's trust nobody up top closes the lower locks behind you. And a man who spent the whole descent refusing to kill anything finds his hand won't close on the plunger.
outcomes.narration: You wedge the charges into the Undergate's hinges and run. The roof comes down on the source with a sound you feel in your teeth, and the river goes back to being buried, under rock this time instead of brick. Within a week the Chapel Well runs dry, Teo's turbine stops, and the Ward drinks from council tankers at council prices. A month later the council takes down the wall and calls it a success; Ines stands at the gap and doesn't cheer. Whatever was still in the lower galleries is still there. End of the prologue.
outcomes.verdict: You chose a wall you could trust over a river you couldn't, and paid for it in water.

fates.text: Keeps the locks. Never thanks you. Never needs to.
Home, limping, driving the council's water tanker.
You carried him out on your back as the roof came down. Ines never asks how close it was.
He was still in the east gallery when the roof came down. Ines told everyone he got out. The council's survey crew finds him in the spring, and she stops telling people anything.
The turbine stops. He leaves the day the wall comes down, owing everyone.
Walks out the day the wall opens. He doesn't wave.
Never speaks to you again. Moves across the city, near a river that still runs in the open.
Not dead. Gods don't die of rock. Waiting.

outcomes.title: The Engine
outcomes.intent: Bind the god: make the beaten Gonggong sign Teo's ledger and turn the turbines; harness the river for the Ward.
outcomes.ifUnmet: A god signs only on his back, and only for a man who knows how to keep demons working: without the ledger, without beating him, without a crew of your own and Teo's trust, the ink won't take.
outcomes.narration: Gonggong, on his back in the flood, signs Teo's ledger with a finger of river water, and the ink takes. By morning every turbine in the Ward is turning; there is light in Sump Row for the first time in five weeks and clean water from every tap. The Undergate stays open by contract, and every week a few more demons come up it and are put to work hauling, lighting, pumping. The council looks at a Ward full of bound demons and adds a second ring of wire to the wall. Teo is the most important man in the Ward now, and he makes sure everyone knows who brought him the god. End of the prologue.
outcomes.verdict: You chose a light that someone has to keep paying for, and let the man who broke the gate hold the bill.

fates.text: The Ward knows he wedged the gate. They pay for his light anyway.
Nobody ever learns who wedged the gate. Teo makes sure of it.
Refuses the light. Sits in the Lock House by candle, keeping locks nobody uses.
His crew splits: half take Pumphouse jobs, half keep chipping at a wall that just got thicker.
Sits by the turbine intake listening to the river turn wheels. She says it sounds like weeping.
Teo's crew finds him in the east gallery when they come down to service the intakes. He works for Teo again, and hates it.
A god in harness. Patient. Contracts end.

outcomes.title: The River Comes Home
outcomes.intent: Give the river back: let Gonggong take his old bed, open the culverts, let the Sallow run in daylight and the demons go home.
outcomes.ifUnmet: The god only takes his river home gently for a man who spoke to him instead of beating him, who spared some of his children on the way down, and whom Hester's people trust enough to pull up the culvert grates.
outcomes.narration: You stand aside, and Gonggong takes the gate in his coils and opens it like a door. The Sallow comes up its old bed under the Ward, lifting the culverts out of the ground brick by brick, and by dawn it runs in daylight for the first time in ninety years, straight down Sump Row. The wall breaks where the river crosses it, and no council on earth can wall up a river; the demons go back into the water with their god. Sump Row is gone. The Ward is two halves now, with a river between them. End of the prologue.
outcomes.verdict: You gave the river back its room, and took it from the people who were living there.

fates.text: Stands on the new bank and weeps, for both reasons.
Runs the relief kitchen on Chapel Hill for a month, sleeves rolled up, counting every family twice.
Everyone got out. They lost everything they couldn't carry up the hill.
Not everyone got out. The man who swept his step every morning is never found.
Her locks are under ten feet of river. She leaves the Ward.
The turbine hall floods; the Pumphouse is a shell. He sells candles.
His crew walks out through the gap the river made. Half of them walk back.
The river carries him up into the daylight half-drowned and puts him down on the new bank.
He tips his head to you as he goes, once. From a god, that is a great deal.

outcomes.title: The Breach
outcomes.intent: Break out: send the flood at the wall, let Dario blow it, walk the whole Ward out with the water.
outcomes.ifUnmet: Dario needs a charge in his hand and a reason to believe you; and a man who ran from every fight down there doesn't get followed through a hole in a wall.
outcomes.narration: You turn the flood down the old culvert towards the wall and shout up the drain, and up in the Ward Dario lights the fuse. The wall goes out in one long breath of concrete and water, and the whole Ward walks out through the gap with the flood around its ankles: old men, kids, cats in boxes, demons. The council's lines break; nobody can hold a wall that isn't there. On the other side is a city that never wanted them, and no one is waiting with rooms. The Ward as a place is over; the Ward as people walks on into the city, together, for now. End of the prologue.
outcomes.verdict: You chose the people over the place, and found out how much of them was the place.

fates.text: He keeps looking for his sister in a crowd she isn't in. The people he lied to don't forgive him for weeks.
They came knowing nobody was waiting. That is worth more to him than he can say, and he tries to say it to you anyway.
Somebody has to keep the locks. She's still there when the water goes down.
Pell carries her bag. She doesn't look back at the Lock House, which is how you know it costs her.
Loads his generator on a cart and sells light to the refugees at a fair price, for once.
Goes back down to the river alone.
The flood carries him out through the breach. He finds the Ward empty and his mother gone ahead.
His river runs out into the city's drains. He follows it.

outcomes.title: Everybody's Man
outcomes.intent: Try to give everyone something: a compromise, a channel for the river, the pumps kept, the wall opened, all at once; or simply having promised everyone.
outcomes.narration: Everyone acts on what you told them, at the same moment. Ines's people slam the lower locks shut, Teo throws every turbine lever open, Dario's crew is at the wall with whatever they have, and Hester's people haul up the culvert grates to let the river through. The water has four places to go and goes to all of them badly: the turbine hall floods and collapses, the locks burst, Sump Row goes under, and the wall holds. By morning nobody has what they wanted, everybody has lost something, and every one of them remembers that you promised. Somewhere in the cistern, a god is laughing. End of the prologue.
outcomes.verdict: You tried to make room for everyone. There wasn't room.

fates.text: Caught in the lower lock when it burst. She lives. She doesn't speak to you.
The turbine hall is rubble. He tells everyone whose idea it was.
The wall held. His crew scattered. He waits for you to explain, and you can't.
Sits on the drowned grate on Sump Row with her notebook shut.
Still in the east gallery when four kinds of water came at once.
Sells to all of them the next morning. 'Told you, love.'
Laughing in the cistern. He'll be back.

outcomes.title: High Water
outcomes.intent: Fallback. Waiting, hesitating, refusing to choose, walking away to save himself, or asking for something his record makes impossible.
outcomes.narration: You don't choose, so the water does. The Undergate fails on its own and the river takes the lowest road it can find: the Pumphouse floods to the rafters, Sump Row goes under to the windowsills, and the wall holds. Nobody's plan happens; nobody's plan is stopped, either. The council sends pumps a week later and keeps the wall up another year to be sure. Everyone in the Ward remembers that you were the one standing in front of the gate. End of the prologue.
outcomes.verdict: You kept every door open until the water closed them.

fates.text: Waits for the council's next terms. She's good at waiting. She hates it.
Pumps out the Pumphouse and starts again, smaller.
Keeps chipping at the wall.
Stays down in the culverts with her stone, talking to the river, which isn't listening.
The council's pump crews find him a week later, alive, just.
Still open. 'Somebody has to be.'
Half his river is in the Ward's cellars now. He is in no hurry.

reflections.text: You talked to everything that would listen, human or not. Words got you further down than swords would have. Up here, people call that stalling.
You killed a great many of the things that came up with the water. Somebody had to. You never asked who decided that.
You barely raised a hand to anything down there. You came up with a crew instead, and nobody in the Ward could tell any more whose side they were on.
You let a lot of them walk away. Mercy is a position too. It costs whoever they walk into next.
You ran when it went bad, more than once. Running keeps every option open. So does standing still.
You caught people lying to you, and it didn't make choosing any easier. The truth almost never does.
Everyone lied to you a little, and you never caught them. That's not a crime. It's how most people get through a flood.
You said yes to almost everyone. It felt like kindness at the time.
You never promised anyone anything. Nobody could hold you to it, and nobody could count on you.
At the drain shed you stepped past and let them sort it out. Ines's wrist remembers.
At the drain shed you cut the difference, and handed two people half a bridge each.
At the drain shed you picked Ines, early and out loud, in front of a boy who'd have followed you anywhere.
At the drain shed you picked Dario, early and out loud, in front of a woman who'd kept the water off your street for thirty years.
You never went looking for the knocking. Somebody down there was counting days.

coda: Every plan in the Ward was a way of choosing what to make room for: the wall, the light, the river, the people. Each of them was right about something. Each of them, pushed all the way, pushed something else out.
So did you. That was always going to be the price of standing in front of the gate.
engineNotes: Conditions everywhere use the engine's meets() format: { flags: { f: true|false }, meters: { m: { min, max } } }. An unset flag counts as false; meters start at 0.
Map entities use showIf for conditional visibility (alternatives may share a tile when their showIf conditions exclude each other). Triggers use requires. Stairs use toX/toY.

NEW entity type 'demon' (ward kettle, culvert leprechaun, cistern Furfur, south-hall banshee): a visible, blocking, fixed demon. Bump: play its scene once, then open the normal demon talk/fight encounter with that demon at that level (talk can end in join, leave, pass, gift or a fight; escape allowed). Any resolution sets its flag (each has showIf flag false, so it disappears). talkNote is extra direction for this encounter, appended to the demon's card in the talk prompt.

Boss entity: flag (set on any resolution), winFlag 'gonggong_beaten' (set only if he is beaten in battle; the_engine and river_home depend on it), talkFlag 'gonggong_heard' (set if talk ends peacefully), talkNote (as for demon entities), after 'finale_intro', finale true.

Scene choices may carry give (item id added to inventory), take (item id removed) and learn (fact ids added to story.facts, so NPC lies with truthFact can be caught in free talk). Flags carry all story logic; the items are for the inventory and flavour.
Speakers that are not NPC names: 'Kettle' (tanuki), 'Leprechaun', 'Furfur', 'Banshee', 'Gonggong' (demon portraits).

Outcome extra fields for the director: intent (what the player has to say to aim at it), ifUnmet (why it is impossible when its requires fail), verdict (one-line SMT I-style judgment). Show the matching reflections (requires met, up to three) and the coda after the narration.
